summary:
The shell is finished. It provides the two workspaces and the map-first Public/Command layout, and it builds, typechecks, lints and tests clean.

- **Workspaces:** `App.tsx` mounts only the active workspace. Forensic (the existing R3F scene and panels, unchanged) is lazy-loaded with a workspace switch. Public/Command is one MapLibre map with floating chrome. Switching workspace, preset or perspective keeps the incident, forecast run, timeline time, data mode, selection and view centre. The camera hand-off goes through `ui/shell/handoff.ts`.
- **Layout:** compact header (incident picker, workspace and preset switches, demo badge for fixtures only, Analysis and Layers toggles, an incident-ID chip in Command), search, map controls, a collapsible right updates panel (Command adds a Data status block with each source's newest time), the coordinate strip, the compact timeline, the legend, the research-prototype note and the credits.
- **Drawers:** an Analysis drawer holds the three existing charts (closed by default). A Layers & settings drawer holds basemap, wildfire layers, optional sources, forecast run, units and a pointer to Forensic.
- **Safe area:** every floating region is a `[data-chrome]` slot. `useMapSafeArea` turns the docked ones into `--safe-*` CSS vars and `useWorkspace.safeInsets`, which map-core uses as map padding.
- **Map share at 1440x900, default view:** Public leaves 75.1-76.8 % of the map unobstructed on all 10 bundles. Command leaves 62.5-66.0 %, because it is denser by design.
- **Narrow screens:** one bottom sheet at a time. Search, coordinates and timeline stay visible. On phones in Command the coordinate strip starts clamped, with a toggle. A header menu holds the workspace, preset and panel switches.
- **Keyboard and motion:** skip links, the map after the chrome in tab order, visible focus rings, Escape closes the newest drawer and returns focus, and `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected.
- **This session (resume):** the research-prototype note now sits on a dark glass chip, so it is readable on the Roads basemap and aerial imagery (map-core had flagged it). I removed fallback CSS for skeleton classes that no longer exist. I re-measured coverage on all bundles, re-ran every behaviour check, and re-took and reviewed all 27 screenshots.

contract_deviations: Additive notes in CONTRACT §3.1 (shell implementation notes), updated with this session's numbers. Covers `[data-chrome]` + `--chrome-side` for the safe area, the `.mw` state classes and layout vars, CoordsSlot clamping, the phone sheet rules and the drawer keyboard model.

The 75 % target is met for the default Public view (no point selected, no drawer open) on every bundle. Command's default view is 62.5-66.0 %: its Data status block (source timestamps) and full coordinate strip (DMS, UTM, IDs, record times) are the extra density the brief asks Command to show. Pressing H hides the panels (84 %).

With a point selected, the location card and the updates panel are both visible, as in Image 1. That gives 67.6 % (Public) and 55.3 % (Command) at 1440x900. I did not auto-collapse the updates panel when a point is selected (location's suggestion), because closing a panel the user opened on a map click would be surprising.

Phones: the updates panel starts closed (a header toggle opens it as a sheet), only one sheet is open at a time, and the legend moves into the Layers sheet. At 761-1279 px, Analysis and Layers become icon-only and the Command ID chip is hidden; the coordinate strip still shows the ID.
`web/src/state/store.ts` and `web/src/state/workspace.ts` were not changed; the existing `panelsCollapsed` / `setPanelsCollapsed` and the foundation workspace store were enough.
known_issues: At 1024 px in Command, the reported coordinates wrap onto two lines (latitude / longitude, location's `.is-tight` mode). The bottom row there holds the 420 px timeline minimum, the legend and the tall Command strip. Capping the legend did not avoid the wrap.

fixture-live (75.1 %) and Madre (75.7 %) are closest to the 75 % line. Their legends wrap to two rows next to the 480 px minimum timeline. A taller timeline or legend from timeline-feed or map-core could push them below 75 %. Re-run `kb/coverage.mjs` after such changes.
The Forensic workspace switch (top-left under the compass) can sit over the 3D ignition label on phones (`redesign-shell-forensic-390.png`). The Forensic header itself is out of scope this round.
The OpenStreetMap/Mapterhorn credit line is map-core's. It is readable but long; on phones it takes three lines at the bottom.
notes_for_integrator:
1. **Mount points** are in `App.tsx` `MapWorkspace`:
   - `.mw-search` → SearchBox
   - `.mw-card` → LocationCard
   - `.mw-controls` → MapControls
   - `.mw-updates` → UpdatesPanel wrapping UpdatesFeed
   - `CoordsSlot` → CoordinateStrip
   - `.mw-timeline` → CompactTimeline
   - `.mw-legend-slot` → MapLegend
   - `.mw-footer-attrib` → MapAttribution
   - The LayersPanel and AnalysisDrawer slots.

   A new floating element (for example an evacuation or camera panel from optional-sources) only needs `data-chrome="<name>"` and a CSS `--chrome-side` (`top|right|bottom|left|none`, per breakpoint). It is then included in the safe area, the map padding and `window.__mapChrome()`. The optional-sources toggles already live in `LayersPanel.tsx` (it reads `mapLayers.evacuation/cameras/recentImagery`).
2. **Switching** always goes through `switchWorkspace()` (`ui/shell/handoff.ts`). Only the active workspace is mounted.
3. **Phone sheets:** `SHEETS` in `App.tsx` lists the bottom sheets (updates, layers, analysis), and only one is open at a time on phones. A new sheet-like panel should join that list and use `useDrawerFocus` (`ui/shell/hooks.ts`), so Escape and focus return keep working.
4. **Re-checking:** scratch scripts in the session scratchpad expect Vite on 5182; change the base URL for other ports.
   - `kb/coverage.mjs <base> <w> <h> [public|command] "" -- <ids…>`: coverage per incident.
   - `s4/finals.sh`: the 27 shell screenshots.
   - `kb/roundtrip.mjs`, `kb/keys.mjs`, `kb/motion.mjs`, `kb/coords-clamp.mjs`.
5. **Dev handles:** `window.__mapChrome()` returns `{ insets, unobstructed, items }`, alongside `__store`, `__workspace` and `__mapRuntime`.
6. **Untouched processes:** the Vite server on 5180 and the fixture API on 8720 were already running. They are not mine, and I left them alone.
